content: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that enables systems to learn and improve from experience without explicit programming. Reinforcement learning (RL) specifically focuses on how agents take actions in environments to maximize cumulative rewards. Unlike supervised learning (which requires labeled training data) or unsupervised learning (which finds patterns in unlabeled data), RL learns optimal behavior through trial-and-error interactions with the environment. The core components of reinforcement learning include: the agent (the decision-maker), the environment (everything the agent interacts with), states (specific situations the agent can be in), actions (choices available to the agent), and rewards (numerical feedback signals). The agent's goal is to learn a policyâa strategy for choosing actions based on statesâthat maximizes expected cumulative rewards over time. This optimization involves balancing exploration (trying new actions to discover their outcomes) with exploitation (choosing actions known to yield high rewards). Key RL algorithms include Q-learning, which builds a table of state-action values (Q-values) that estimate the expected future rewards for taking a specific action in a specific state. Deep reinforcement learning combines RL principles with deep neural networks to handle more complex environments with high-dimensional state spaces, enabling breakthroughs in areas like game playing (AlphaGo) and robotics.

scenario.title: Virtual Pet Trainer
scenario.content: Students train virtual pets to perform tricks using reinforcement learning principles. The simulation provides pets with varying learning capabilities and students with different training tools like treats (positive reinforcement), clickers (signals), and environmental modifications. Students design reward structures, action sequences, and training regimens to shape their pet's behavior toward desired outcomes. The system visualizes the pet's internal learning process, showing how neural connections strengthen over training sessions and how Q-values or policy networks evolve. Interactive tools allow students to adjust learning parameters like learning rate, discount factor, and exploration rate to observe their effects on training efficiency. Challenge modes require students to train pets with different learning styles or to achieve complex behaviors through carefully structured incremental training, teaching fundamental principles of behavior shaping and policy optimization.

hypothesis.description: Students will implement reinforcement learning strategies by designing effective reward systems and training protocols. They will analyze how feedback timing and consistency affect learning efficiency, and develop incremental approaches to train complex behaviors through component skills.
